# equipe

> equipe is an open-source AI software squad: a team of role-based agents (PM, Designer, Frontend, Backend, Mobile, QA and Data) that works on your repository through a shared board, in isolated git worktrees, and waits for a person's approval before anything merges. It is the team layer on top of existing agent engines (Codex and Claude Code today), not another agent loop. Early-stage, MIT licensed.

## How it works

- Roles: each member has a role with a model suited to it and its own memory.
- Tickets: the board is the single source of truth; members coordinate through tickets and immutable events, not chat.
- Branches: each member works in its own git worktree on its own branch, so several can work at once without touching your checkout.
- Your approval: nothing merges until the person leading the squad says so.
- Apps: a desktop app (macOS) and a mobile app (iOS and Android) are coming soon; they are not released yet.

## Get started

Install a prebuilt `equipe` on macOS or Linux (it goes in `~/.local/bin`, checked against its SHA-256):

    curl -fsSL https://github.com/equipe-labs/equipe/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh

Or with Homebrew:

    brew install equipe-labs/tap/equipe

To build from source instead you need Rust 1.88+ and git (the Claude engine also needs the `claude` binary):

    git clone https://github.com/equipe-labs/equipe && cd equipe
    cargo install --locked --path crates/cli

Then:

    equipe login     # sign in to Codex or Claude Code
    equipe status    # check engine readiness and model availability
    equipe           # open the squad console
